bc1.title: Think Like a Free Agent
bc1.intro: Karim hears that a competitor has cut its service team and starts worrying about his job. His manager Mona explains how to protect his career by thinking like a free agent.
bc1.introAr: كريم بيسمع إن شركة منافسة استغنت عن فريق الصيانة بتاعها ويبدأ يقلق على شغله. مديرته منى بتشرح له إزاي يحمي مستقبله المهني لما يفكر زي الـ ‎free agent‎.

dialogue.en: Mona, did you hear that one of our competitors downsized its whole service team last week? Twenty engineers are gone.
dialogue.ar: يا منى، سمعتي إن واحدة من الشركات المنافسة عملت ‎downsize‎ لفريق الصيانة كله الأسبوع اللي فات؟ عشرين مهندس مشيوا.

dialogue.en: I heard. They had a budget crunch after two big solar projects were delayed, so the cutbacks started with the field staff.
dialogue.ar: سمعت. كان عندهم عجز في الميزانية بعد ما مشروعين طاقة شمسية كبار اتأجلوا، فالتخفيضات بدأت بفريق الموقع.

dialogue.en: It scares me. I always thought that if I worked hard here, I'd have a job for life.
dialogue.ar: الموضوع ده مخوّفني. أنا طول عمري فاكر إني لو اشتغلت بضمير هنا هفضل في الوظيفة دي العمر كله.

dialogue.en: I hate to throw cold water on that idea, but a job for life doesn't really exist anymore. You need a different mindset.
dialogue.ar: مش حابة أحبطك في الفكرة دي، بس الوظيفة اللي على طول العمر مابقتش موجودة خلاص. محتاج طريقة تفكير مختلفة.

dialogue.en: What kind of mindset?
dialogue.ar: طريقة تفكير عاملة إزاي يعني؟

dialogue.en: Think like a free agent. Imagine you're a football player: your skills belong to you, and any team could want you tomorrow.
dialogue.ar: فكّر كأنك ‎free agent‎. تخيّل إنك لاعب كورة: مهاراتك ملكك إنت، وأي فريق ممكن يطلبك بكرة.

dialogue.en: So you're telling me to look for another job?
dialogue.ar: يعني إنتي بتقولي لي أدوّر على شغل تاني؟

dialogue.en: Not at all. A free agent can stay loyal and still manage his own career. It's about being business minded, not about leaving.
dialogue.ar: خالص. الـ ‎free agent‎ ممكن يفضل مخلص لشركته وفي نفس الوقت هو اللي بيدير مستقبله. الفكرة إنك تفكر بعقلية رجل أعمال، مش إنك تمشي.

dialogue.en: What does business minded mean for a service engineer like me?
dialogue.ar: يعني إيه أفكر بعقلية رجل أعمال لمهندس صيانة زيي؟

dialogue.en: It means you treat yourself like a small company. What do you sell? Who are your customers? And what do you bring to the table that others don't?
dialogue.ar: يعني تعامل نفسك كأنك شركة صغيرة. بتبيع إيه؟ مين عملاءك؟ وإيه اللي إنت بتضيفه وغيرك مابيضيفوش؟

dialogue.en: Well, I can repair UPS units and replace battery banks quickly.
dialogue.ar: بصراحة أنا بصلّح أجهزة ‎UPS‎ وبغيّر مجموعات البطاريات بسرعة.

dialogue.en: Good, but many engineers can do that. Time for a reality check: do you understand the total picture, how cooling, power and servers in a data centre depend on each other?
dialogue.ar: كويس، بس مهندسين كتير يقدروا يعملوا كده. خلينا نبقى واقعيين: إنت فاهم الصورة كاملة؟ إزاي التبريد والكهربا والسيرفرات في الداتا سنتر معتمدين على بعض؟

dialogue.en: Honestly, not really. I mostly stay in the battery room.
dialogue.ar: بصراحة لأ أوي. أنا أغلب الوقت قاعد في أوضة البطاريات.

dialogue.en: That's the problem. Don't stay secluded in one corner. Spend a day with the VFD team and ask the sales people how they price a solar plant.
dialogue.ar: هي دي المشكلة. ماتفضلش منعزل في ركن واحد. اقعد يوم مع فريق الـ ‎VFD‎ واسأل ناس المبيعات بيسعّروا محطة الطاقة الشمسية إزاي.

dialogue.en: And that will help me move up the ranks?
dialogue.ar: وده هيساعدني أترقى وأطلع لقدام؟

dialogue.en: Over time, yes. Also, build your brand. When a hospital calls and asks for the engineer who fixed their UPS in one night, that's your brand.
dialogue.ar: مع الوقت آه. وكمان ابني اسمك. لما مستشفى تتصل وتطلب المهندس اللي صلّح الـ ‎UPS‎ بتاعهم في ليلة واحدة، ده هو الـ ‎brand‎ بتاعك.

dialogue.en: That actually happened last month at a clinic in Nasr City!
dialogue.ar: ده حصل فعلاً الشهر اللي فات في عيادة في مدينة نصر!

dialogue.en: Exactly. Now make it happen on purpose. Share short case studies on LinkedIn and generate a buzz about the work you do.
dialogue.ar: بالظبط. دلوقتي خليه يحصل وإنت قاصد. انشر قصص قصيرة عن شغلك على ‎LinkedIn‎ وخلّي الناس تتكلم عن اللي بتعمله.

dialogue.en: Isn't that showing off?
dialogue.ar: مش ده يبقى استعراض؟

dialogue.en: Not if it's useful. Be a purple cow, the engineer people remember because he's different, not because he's loud.
dialogue.ar: لأ، طالما مفيد. خليك ‎purple cow‎، المهندس اللي الناس فاكراه عشان مختلف، مش عشان صوته عالي.

dialogue.en: What else should I do?
dialogue.ar: أعمل إيه كمان؟

dialogue.en: Join a trade organization, like a solar energy association. You'll meet engineers from many companies and learn things you'd never see here.
dialogue.ar: اشترك في جمعية مهنية، زي جمعية للطاقة الشمسية. هتقابل مهندسين من شركات كتير وتتعلم حاجات عمرك ما هتشوفها هنا.

dialogue.en: Okay. I'll write a plan this week and actually implement it, not just talk about it.
dialogue.ar: تمام. هكتب خطة الأسبوع ده وهنفذها بجد، مش مجرد كلام.

dialogue.en: That's the spirit. It won't pay off in a month, but in two or three years you'll see the difference.
dialogue.ar: هو ده الكلام. مش هتجيب نتيجة في شهر، بس بعد سنتين تلاتة هتشوف الفرق.

vocab.ar: شخص حر ينقل بمهاراته لأي شركة
vocab.def: A worker who is free to move to any company that values his skills.
vocab.eg: After ten years with inverters, Hany sees himself as a free agent in the solar market.

vocab.def: To say an idea is unrealistic and kill the excitement about it.
vocab.eg: The finance manager threw cold water on our plan to buy a second crane truck.

vocab.def: Your attitude and set of beliefs about something.
vocab.eg: A service engineer with a customer-first mindset answers the phone even on Friday.

vocab.def: Thinking about costs, customers and value like a businessperson does.
vocab.eg: She is very business minded; she always asks how a repair affects the client's profit.

vocab.def: A special name or reputation that makes people choose you over others.
vocab.eg: His brand in the company is 'the man who never leaves a site with a problem'.

vocab.def: A situation where there isn't enough money in the budget.
vocab.eg: Because of the budget crunch, we postponed the new battery tester until next year.

vocab.def: Reductions in spending, such as fewer staff or less advertising.
vocab.eg: The cutbacks meant only one engineer could attend the training in Dubai.

vocab.def: To reduce the number of employees, usually to save money.
vocab.eg: When the factory downsized, it also cancelled its UPS maintenance contract.

vocab.def: A group of people from many companies in the same field who share knowledge.
vocab.eg: I met our biggest client at a trade organization event for data-centre professionals.

vocab.def: Alone and away from other people.
vocab.eg: Don't stay secluded in the workshop; visit the sales office and learn what customers ask for.

vocab.def: An understanding of the whole situation, not only one small part.
vocab.eg: To design a good solar plant, you need the total picture: roof, load, budget and grid.

vocab.def: Something so unusual and remarkable that people notice and remember it.
vocab.eg: Our 2-hour emergency response is a purple cow; no competitor offers it.

vocab.def: To put a plan or decision into action.
vocab.eg: We implemented a new checklist, and battery failures dropped by half.

vocab.def: To get promoted to higher positions step by step.
vocab.eg: Sara started as a technician and moved up the ranks to service manager.

vocab.def: An honest look at a situation, including your weaknesses.
vocab.eg: The failed tender was a reality check: our proposal was too technical and too long.

vocab.def: To create excitement and positive talk about something or someone.
vocab.eg: The video of our 1 MW solar plant generated a buzz among local factory owners.

vocab.def: To offer something useful, such as skills, experience or contacts.
vocab.eg: Mahmoud brings to the table ten years of experience with large VFDs.

vocab.def: To bring a good result after effort or time.
vocab.eg: All those night shifts paid off when the bank renewed our contract.

bc2.title: Writing a Strong Resume
bc2.intro: A bank client wants the resumes of the engineers on a new data-centre project, and Karim's resume is years old. Mona shows him how to turn a list of duties into real achievements.
bc2.introAr: بنك عميل عايز الـ ‎CV‎ بتاع المهندسين اللي هيشتغلوا على مشروع داتا سنتر جديد، والـ ‎CV‎ بتاع كريم قديم من سنين. منى بتوريه إزاي يحوّل قايمة المهام لإنجازات حقيقية.

dialogue.en: Karim, the bank wants the resumes of every engineer on the data-centre project. Can you send me yours by Thursday?
dialogue.ar: يا كريم، البنك عايز الـ ‎CV‎ بتاع كل مهندس في مشروع الداتا سنتر. تقدر تبعتلي بتاعك قبل الخميس؟

dialogue.en: Sure, but mine is really out of date. The last time I touched it was right after graduation.
dialogue.ar: أكيد، بس بتاعي قديم أوي. آخر مرة فتحته كان بعد التخرج على طول.

dialogue.en: Then this is a good chance to fix it. Keep a copy for yourself too; the new site supervisor job opens in January.
dialogue.ar: يبقى دي فرصة كويسة تظبطه. واحتفظ بنسخة لنفسك كمان، وظيفة مشرف الموقع الجديدة هتفتح في يناير.

dialogue.en: Really? I heard something about it over the water cooler, but I wasn't sure.
dialogue.ar: بجد؟ أنا سمعت كلام عنها في الدردشة بين الزملاء بس ماكنتش متأكد.

dialogue.en: It's true. Management approved one extra head count for our department. So what's in your resume right now?
dialogue.ar: صح. الإدارة وافقت على عدد موظف زيادة لقسمنا. طب الـ ‎CV‎ بتاعك فيه إيه دلوقتي؟

dialogue.en: A list of jobs and duties: responsible for UPS maintenance, responsible for battery replacement, and so on.
dialogue.ar: قايمة بالوظايف والمهام: مسؤول عن صيانة الـ ‎UPS‎، مسؤول عن تغيير البطاريات، وهكذا.

dialogue.en: That tells the reader what you were supposed to do, not what you achieved. The big ticket item in any resume is concrete accomplishments.
dialogue.ar: ده بيقول للي بيقرا إنت كان المفروض تعمل إيه، مش إنت حققت إيه. أهم حاجة في أي ‎CV‎ هي الإنجازات الملموسة.

dialogue.en: Such as?
dialogue.ar: زي إيه مثلاً؟

dialogue.en: Numbers and results. How many sites did you cover? Did you reduce downtime? Did you save a customer money?
dialogue.ar: أرقام ونتايج. غطيت كام موقع؟ قللت وقت التوقف؟ وفّرت فلوس لعميل؟

dialogue.en: Well, last year I coordinated the battery replacement at the Alexandria factory: 240 batteries in one weekend with zero downtime.
dialogue.ar: بصي، السنة اللي فاتت نسّقت تغيير البطاريات في مصنع إسكندرية: 240 بطارية في ويك إند واحد من غير أي توقف.

dialogue.en: Perfect. Write exactly that. And no fluff like hard-working team player; everybody writes that.
dialogue.ar: ممتاز. اكتبها كده بالظبط. ومن غير كلام حشو زي ‎hard-working team player‎، ده الكل بيكتبه.

dialogue.en: What about my training? I finished a VFD course and a solar installation course.
dialogue.ar: وبالنسبة للكورسات؟ أنا خلّصت كورس ‎VFD‎ وكورس تركيب طاقة شمسية.

dialogue.en: Include them, but keep it short. The bank cares more about your track record on real sites than about certificates.
dialogue.ar: حطهم، بس باختصار. البنك يهمه تاريخك وخبرتك في مواقع حقيقية أكتر من الشهادات.

dialogue.en: How long should it be? Two pages? Three?
dialogue.ar: المفروض يبقى طوله قد إيه؟ صفحتين؟ تلاتة؟

dialogue.en: One page is ideal, two at most. Treat it like a sales pitch: short, clear and focused on what the reader needs.
dialogue.ar: صفحة واحدة أحسن حاجة، وبالكتير صفحتين. اتعامل معاه كأنه عرض بيع: قصير وواضح ومركّز على اللي القارئ محتاجه.

dialogue.en: Got it. And the supervisor interview? I haven't been an interviewee since my first job, and that interview was traumatic.
dialogue.ar: فهمت. وبالنسبة لإنترفيو المشرف؟ أنا مادخلتش إنترفيو من أول شغلانة، والإنترفيو ده كان صدمة بصراحة.

dialogue.en: Everyone has a story like that! Remember, the interviewer will have your resume in front of him, so be ready to explain every line.
dialogue.ar: كلنا عندنا حكاية زي دي! افتكر إن اللي بيعمل الإنترفيو هيبقى الـ ‎CV‎ بتاعك قدامه، فخليك جاهز تشرح كل سطر.

dialogue.en: So I need to know the nuts and bolts of each project I mention.
dialogue.ar: يعني لازم أكون عارف التفاصيل الأساسية لكل مشروع هذكره.

dialogue.en: Exactly: the budget, the team size, the problems you solved. And check everything; dot your i's and cross your t's. A spelling mistake in uninterruptible looks bad for an engineer.
dialogue.ar: بالظبط: الميزانية، حجم الفريق، المشاكل اللي حليتها. وراجع كل حاجة بدقة. غلطة إملائية في كلمة ‎uninterruptible‎ شكلها وحش على مهندس.

dialogue.en: Ha, I'd better run a spell check. Should I also network with people in other departments before the interview?
dialogue.ar: ها، يبقى أحسن أعمل تدقيق إملائي. وأعمل علاقات مع ناس في الأقسام التانية قبل الإنترفيو؟

dialogue.en: Yes, but naturally. Last year Hany helped the sales team with a technical proposal, and lo and behold, he was the first name they suggested for the key accounts role.
dialogue.ar: آه، بس بشكل طبيعي. السنة اللي فاتت هاني ساعد فريق المبيعات في عرض فني، وفجأة لقيناه أول اسم رشحوه لوظيفة كبار العملاء.

dialogue.en: That's a useful lesson. I'll send you the new resume on Wednesday.
dialogue.ar: درس مفيد. هبعتلك الـ ‎CV‎ الجديد يوم الأربع.

dialogue.en: Great. And don't let it get old again: update it every time you finish a big project.
dialogue.ar: هايل. وماتسيبوش يقدم تاني: حدّثه كل ما تخلّص مشروع كبير.

vocab.def: A short document listing your work history, skills and achievements.
vocab.eg: Before the tender, every engineer updated his resume with his latest data-centre projects.

vocab.def: Old and no longer correct or useful.
vocab.eg: The wiring diagram in the panel was out of date, so we drew a new one.

vocab.def: In informal chat between colleagues at work.
vocab.eg: News of the new solar contract spread over the water cooler before the official email.

vocab.def: The number of people working in a team or company.
vocab.eg: We need more head count in maintenance because we signed twelve new contracts.

vocab.def: The most important or most valuable part of something.
vocab.eg: The big ticket item in this quotation is the 400 kVA UPS, not the cables.

vocab.def: Real, specific results you can prove, often with numbers.
vocab.eg: Cutting the site's diesel use by 30% is one of her concrete accomplishments.

vocab.def: Words that sound nice but add no real information.
vocab.eg: Remove the fluff from the proposal and keep only the technical data and prices.

vocab.def: To organize people or tasks so they work well together.
vocab.eg: Karim coordinated the crane, the electricians and the client's IT team for the installation.

vocab.def: Your past performance, showing how well you have done a job.
vocab.eg: Our track record of 50 hospital UPS installations helped us win the contract.

vocab.def: A short, persuasive talk or text that tries to sell something.
vocab.eg: His sales pitch to the factory owner focused on savings from the new VFDs.

vocab.def: The person who is being interviewed for a job.
vocab.eg: The interviewee brought photos of the solar plants he had installed.

vocab.def: Very upsetting and difficult to forget.
vocab.eg: The server-room fire was a traumatic night for the whole team.

vocab.def: The person who asks the questions in an interview.
vocab.eg: The interviewer asked me how I would handle an angry client during a blackout.

vocab.def: The basic, practical details of how something works.
vocab.eg: New technicians must learn the nuts and bolts of battery testing before visiting sites.

vocab.w: dot your i's and cross your t's
vocab.def: To check every small detail carefully so nothing is wrong.
vocab.eg: Before submitting the tender, dot your i's and cross your t's; one wrong price can lose it.

vocab.def: To meet and build relationships with people who can help your career.
vocab.eg: I networked with the data-centre team at the exhibition and got two new leads.

vocab.def: Used before saying a surprising result.
vocab.eg: We cleaned the inverter's fans, and lo and behold, the overheating alarm stopped.
